  ▶ Checking prerequisites...

Every other tool in the suite ships prebuilt artifacts — compare beadle, which downloads a versioned tarball and verifies it:

  ▶ Downloading beadle-email v0.16.4...
  ▶ Verifying checksum...

Problems with the source-build path:
1. Hard dependency on a Go toolchain being present. On a host without Go, install.sh has no path to a working ethos at all.
2. No integrity verification. The beadle path does SHA256; a `go build` from a git checkout has no equivalent gate.
3. Slow, and the cost is paid on every reinstall — install-all.sh reinstalls unconditionally.
4. "(fallback build)" reads as a warning the operator can do nothing about, because the primary path does not exist for this platform.

Work: add a goreleaser (or equivalent) release job publishing per-platform archives + a SHA256SUMS file to GitHub Releases, and teach install.sh to prefer download-and-verify, keeping the Go build as a genuine last resort. Match beadle install.sh’s download/verify structure so the two read alike.

Platform matrix to cover at minimum: linux/amd64, linux/arm64, darwin/arm64, darwin/amd64.

Observed: install-all.sh run 2026-08-28, ethos 4.15.0, host Ubuntu 24.04 / linux-amd64 with Go 1.26 present.' 2>&1 | tail -5

tool_input.text: The root cause isn't the submodule. Ethos enable deposits its guide, setup doc, manifest, and marker inside dot punt-labs slash ethos — the same directory that is the shared registry mount. So that one path is both the read surface, owned by the team repo, and the write surface, owned by each consuming repo. A submodule turns those per-repo writes into writes against a foreign repo, and the guard correctly refuses. Every other tool owns its own directory outright, which is why only ethos breaks. Two things you should know. First, the cost is bigger than a failed enable — audit sealing is blocked the same way, so all seventeen submodule repos have no working audit trail, and deleting one of those checkouts destroys unsealed records. Second, your fleet has two incompatible inline target states already running: tracked bespoke data in vox and lux, versus gitignored global resolution in quarry, punt-kit, and z-spec. I recommend tracked bespoke, per your earlier ruling. Confirm that and I'll write the migration plan.

tool_input.text: You were right to push back — read versus write was the wrong axis. Every tool reads and writes its own directory. The real distinction is shared across repos versus per checkout. The vox directory holds only data specific to that one repo. The ethos directory holds both kinds at once: the shared org registry, four hundred sixty-one files identical for every consumer, alongside four per-checkout files — the marker, the manifest, and two guides — whose values must differ per repo. A submodule is one pinned commit, byte identical for everyone who mounts it. That's what a submodule is. So there's nowhere for the per-checkout files to live, and enable has nothing to do but refuse. That's why it's a layout problem, not a git problem. Still waiting on your call between tracked bespoke and gitignored global resolution before I write the migration plan.

tool_input.text: Good news — you don't need a new plan, you need to run an existing one. Ethos vendor is purpose-built for this: it snapshots a self-standing identity set into the repo so it resolves with no global store, paired with resolution repo-only in ethos dot yaml. And the ethos repo itself is already the finished reference implementation. It also explains what you told me about migrated repos carrying everything: vendor pulls the connected component of the team graph, so seeding from a team instead of specific handles drags in most of the roster. Right-sizing happens at seed time, not afterward. One ordering trap — vendor has to read the registry while it's still mounted, but it can't write into a live submodule, so you vendor to a temp directory first, then swap. Before any of that, I need triage: seven repos doing real dev work should vendor a closure, and about nine side projects should probably drop ethos entirely, the way you ruled for dungeon. Confirm those buckets and pick a pilot. I'd suggest mcp-proxy first, then punt-labs root.
